candidates.lead: Stepping Hill's boss says the hospital in Stockport needs "at least £400m" to tackle building issues
candidates.evidence_text: Dad 'held falling lamp' during his wife's labour at Stepping Hill - BBC News Image source, Jules Wilkinson Image caption, Jules Wilkinson holds up a light that he said had fallen from the maternity ward ceiling at Stepping Hill Hospital while his wife was in labour By Kevin Fitzpatrick Greater Manchester political reporter Published 1 hour ago A new father said he had to hold up a light that had fallen from the maternity ward ceiling while his baby was being born below. Jules Wilkinson said the lamp "started to unscrew itself" at Stepping Hill Hospital in Stockport, Greater Manchester, while his wife Lisa was in labour. The hospital's chief executive said Stepping Hill needed "at least £400m" to address building issues while Cheadle MP Tom Morrison said he was raising the matter in Parliament. The government said Stepping Hill was receiving tens of millions of pounds for maintenance and new buildings. Image caption, Scaffolding in the main entrance to Stepping Hill Hospital Wilkinson said: "As my wife is giving birth the lamp started to unscrew itself... almost hits the midwife in the head... and literally falls out the ceiling. "It is on one of these Anglepoise arms and it just unscrewed itself." Wilkinson told BBC North West Tonight he put the lamp on his shoulders "literally hanging on by the chord" and held on to it "for the next hour or so" until his baby had been delivered. He said the maternity suites were "getting on a bit" and recalled how the birthing pools had been out of action because of a lack of heating. But he was keen to stress that "staff are doing their best". Image caption, Karen James, chief executive of the hospital trust, said it needed "at least £400m" to address identified issues Morrison and his fellow Liberal Democrat MP Lisa Smart, who represents nearby Hazel Grove, recently had a "behind the scenes" tour of the hospital. They were shown corridors with ceilings held up by scaffolding and buckets catching rainwater from leaking roofs. "What I've seen is just horrific actually," said Morrison. "This hospital has been badly let down by successive governments and it's time for this government to start acting." Smart added: "Patients are being let down. Staff are not able to give the amazing care that we know they give because the government is not funding the new buildings which would cost far less to run. "And that's what we're calling on the government to deliver." Image caption, Liberal Democrat MPs Tom Morrison and Lisa Smart were shocked by conditions at Stepping Hill Hospital Karen James, chief executive of the Stockport NHS Trust which runs the hospital, said: "Over 65% of our estate are classified in the worst categories and as time goes by the capital stock we've got - the ward areas, the estate as a whole - is getting worse every day." She said many of the buildings from the Victorian era that were not yet collapsing or leaking were also no longer fit for purpose. To meet modern standards for beds and equipment, wards in the main building would need 60% more space so to upgrade them would reduce the number of beds by more than half, she said. Rebecca Chamorto, divisional nurse director for medicine and urgent care, said conditions made life hard for staff and patients. She said: "Staff work in a confined environment with lack of storage and coming in, if it's been raining sometimes, we do get leaks so we have to check. "From a staffing perspective they come in each day with motivation and they deliver really good care despite the environment that they have got." Image caption, Scaffolding on a corridor at Stepping Hill Hospital A Department of Health and Social Care spokesperson said: "This government inherited an overstretched NHS with huge waiting lists and the hospital estate left to crumble. "Whilst decisions about local services are a matter for the local NHS, we are providing the investment and modernisation needed to get patients the care they deserve, in hospital buildings fit for purpose. "In September we confirmed £26m of funding to deliver a new pathology building at Stepping Hill, as well as a further £17m for maintenance and repair schemes, through the estates safety fund - part of £1.5bn confirmed investment so far for projects to address urgent maintenance problems across the NHS estate." They also said the trust had been allocated £75m in "operational capital" to be spent on local priorities over the next four years. Get in touch Tell us which stories we should cover

candidates.summary: More than 40 years after the Falklands War, two veterans reunite for a new documentary
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits.

candidates.lead: More than 40 years after the Falklands War, two veterans reunite for a new documentary
candidates.evidence_text: War veteran returns Falklands helmet to Argentina - BBC News Image source, Mick Dawson Image caption, Andy Gatrick, right, with Hector Pereyra holding his original helmet By George Carden in Rottingdean Published 2 hours ago A former Royal Marine has reunited with an Argentine veteran to return a helmet he "borrowed" during a battle in the Falklands War. Royal Marine Andy Gatrick, who was 18 at the time, came across two injured Argentine soldiers during the Battle of Mount Harriet in 1982. The helmet belonging to one of the men, both of whom were captured by the Marines, had a name on it: Hector. Gatrick, now 63, managed to track him down and flew back on 23 October to return it. He was joined by Mick Dawson, another Royal Marine veteran from Rottingdean, East Sussex, who filmed the exchange for a new documentary called Hector's Helmet. Image source, Andy Gatrick Image caption, Royal Marine veteran Andy Gatrick, left, has returned a helmet he took during the Battle of Mount Harriet "In a very emotional day, he handed the helmet back in person to the guy he could have just as easily killed that night," said Dawson, from Rottingdean in East Sussex. Dawson, 62, told BBC Radio Sussex : "Long story short, our kit was rubbish, we had rubbish helmets that you couldn't wear. We were in berets. "They had good kit, American helmets. He borrowed one of their helmets which belonged to Hector." The two met metres from each other during the Battle of Mount Harriet, which took place on 11 and 12 June, 1982. Gatrick, from Bolton, Greater Manchester, said in footage sent to the BBC: "I put my weapon down and as I bent down to put the strap over my shoulders, I saw movement and a cloth which looked like a white handkerchief. "My eyes adjusted and there was two Argentinians, I didn't know they were badly injured. I dived to the floor, weapon up. [There was] lots of shouting and swearing, bedlam." Image source, George Carden/BBC Image caption, Mick Dawson helped film a documentary of the two veterans reuniting Hector Pereyra welcomed Gatrick and the film crew at his house in Gualeguaychu, eastern Argentina. The two "embraced like long lost brothers", said Dawson, who is originally from Lincolnshire. He added: "I interviewed Hector to get his whole story. I asked him what it was like when he was badly injured and Andy was coming out the darkness. "He said 'I knew this man had the power of life or death over me and he chose life'. That was pretty profound, he then showed me a picture of his nine grandchildren and four children that wouldn't have existed if Andy made a different decision that night. "It was just the most amazing thing to witness." There were 907 total deaths during the 74-day conflict: 649 Argentine military personnel, 255 British personnel and three civilians. Dawson said he hoped to release the documentary next year. Follow BBC Sussex on Facebook , external , X , external , and Instagram , external and listen to BBC Radio Sussex on Sounds . candidates.evidence_text: Stockport Flames shoot into sky as fire breaks out at paper recycling plant 'At one point I thought the whole thing was going to go up' Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 16:31, 10 Nov 2026 View Image The fire broke out on at Elsa Witnesses reported seeing flames shooting into the air as a fire broke out at a paper recycling plant in Stockport . Firefighters were called to Elsa Recycling on Station Road in Reddish this morning It's thought bundles of paper being stored in the yard set alight. Plumes of black smoke were pictured billowing from the blaze Station Road is also thought to have been closed while firefighters battled the flames. candidates.evidence_text: Royal Family Princess of Wales opens up on her cancer and gives recovery update in rare interview 'I was told in hospital that my recovery would not be linear' Add to preferred sources Comments News PA and Paul Britton Reporter 07:47, 11 Nov 2026 View The Princess of Wales has opened up about her recovery from cancer in a rare interview for a magazine guest-edited by her husband, the Prince of Wales Kate spoke to acclaimed author Robert Macfarlane, known for his writings on landscapes and the living world, about finding solace in nature, for a special issue of Country Life. The princess described how nature “doesn’t judge us or expect us to perform”, and echoing remarks she “There will be good days and bad days, that it will take time. This is the same in nature. It shows us that periods of rest, reflection and renewal are equally as important as moments of growth.” She described nature as offering something unique. The future queen said: “It doesn’t ask anything of us. It doesn’t judge us or expect us to perform “It simply allows us to be. It really has been my sanctuary and a place I’ve instinctively wanted to go.”

candidates.evidence_text: Radcliffe Bury council to press ahead with plans to dispose of 'vital' green space despite decision being based on 'flawed' report An earlier report missed out more than half of residents' objections Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richa Bury council will press ahead with plans to dispose of a ‘vital’ community green space despite an original decision being based on a ‘flawed’ and ‘undercooked’ report The authority’s cabinet opted last month to dispose of land known as Milton Meadow, in Radcliffe , to make way for a pupil referral school which could cater for 136 children. The school would be a non-mainstream setting for pupils with additional educational and behavioural needs The town hall does not believe there is an appropriate alternative site for the setting The decision was called in for scrutiny by Radcliffe First councillors Judi Sheppard and Carol Birchmore after they found the report on which the cabinet based their ruling on was missing 28 of the 48 objections lodged by residents Their comments touched on a number of concerns, including loss of the open space, crime, safety, traffic and the impact on residents without gardens. Over recent years, volunteers have spent ‘hundreds of hours’ transforming the land, clearing it, trimming hedges and planting flow

candidates.evidence_text: Trafford Pensioner whose £20k was swiped by thief who travelled 100 miles after spotting Facebook advert speaks of ordeal 'I'm glad he's in jail' Add to preferred sources Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 17:23, 10 Nov 2026 View 4 Images Dav A pensioner whose £20,000 Rolex was swiped by a thief who travelled 100 miles to his Trafford home after spotting his Facebook advert has spoken of the ordeal, saying: "I'm glad he's in jail." David Williams decided to sell his Rolex Daytona Cosmograph Oyster Perpetual watch, which he bought for £20,850 in 2023, to buy a car. The 86-year-old advertised it on Facebook for £18,000, before knocking £1,000 off He got a message from a potential buyer, 'Jack Hilmma', who said he lived in Warrington. 'Jack', who said he lived in Warrington, made a deal with David and agreed to travel to complete the sale 'Jack' was actually Tichine Asan, who lived in Hull. The 27-year-old found out David was elderly and had no relations. David said that when they met, he would be bearing a black overcoat and holding an Age UK bag They arranged the handover for December 15 last year, agreeing on a spot in Sale town centre. David said he believed it was a 'safe place'

Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 16:59, 10 Nov 2026 When Haider Ali started running the notorious Rochdale 'Adam' drugs line, he knew what he was in for. He'd already been jailed for dealing The £1m-a-year racket flooded the streets of the town with crack cocaine and heroin, surviving a series of police operations to bring it down In 2024, two 'untouchable' dealers were the latest to be jailed for running the line, first exposed in the BBC series The Detectives: Taking Down An OCG which shined a light on the gang, based in Newbold, Rochdale. The drugs line became active again within hours of the pair being Ali, 34, was a familiar face on the scene. He was jailed in 2015 after admitting conspiracy to supply heroin and cocaine - one of 13 dealers locked up following an undercover operation In its latest incarnation, Ali - known as 'The Ghost' - ran the 'Adam' line, until he and two others were caught. Monday (November 9), he was jailed for 10 years and six months

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Radcliffe Bury council to press ahead with plans to dispose of 'vital' green space despite decision being based on 'flawed' report An earlier report missed out more than half of residents' objections Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richa Bury council will press ahead with plans to dispose of a ‘vital’ community green space despite an original decision being based on a ‘flawed’ and ‘undercooked’ report The authority’s cabinet opted last month to dispose of land known as Milton Meadow, in Radcliffe , to make way for a pupil referral school which could cater for 136 children. The school would be a non-mainstream setting for pupils with additional educational and behavioural needs The town hall does not believe there is an appropriate alternative site for the setting The decision was called in for scrutiny by Radcliffe First councillors Judi Sheppard and Carol Birchmore after they found the report on which the cabinet based their ruling on was missing 28 of the 48 objections lodged by residents Their comments touched on a number of concerns, including loss of the open space, crime, safety, traffic and the impact on residents without gardens. Over recent years, volunteers have spent ‘hundreds of hours’ transforming the land, clearing it, trimming hedges and planting flow

candidates.evidence_text: Trafford Pensioner whose £20k was swiped by thief who travelled 100 miles after spotting Facebook advert speaks of ordeal 'I'm glad he's in jail' Add to preferred sources Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 17:23, 10 Nov 2026 View 4 Images Dav A pensioner whose £20,000 Rolex was swiped by a thief who travelled 100 miles to his Trafford home after spotting his Facebook advert has spoken of the ordeal, saying: "I'm glad he's in jail." David Williams decided to sell his Rolex Daytona Cosmograph Oyster Perpetual watch, which he bought for £20,850 in 2023, to buy a car. The 86-year-old advertised it on Facebook for £18,000, before knocking £1,000 off He got a message from a potential buyer, 'Jack Hilmma', who said he lived in Warrington. 'Jack', who said he lived in Warrington, made a deal with David and agreed to travel to complete the sale 'Jack' was actually Tichine Asan, who lived in Hull. The 27-year-old found out David was elderly and had no relations. David said that when they met, he would be bearing a black overcoat and holding an Age UK bag They arranged the handover for December 15 last year, agreeing on a spot in Sale town centre. David said he believed it was a 'safe place'

Donna Glynn was caught when police - acting on a tip-off - found nearly £10,000 in cash in a book She claimed her ex-partner was a drug user and that she didn't know, denying her crimes and going to trial. Some of the cocaine found at the Wigan home was 81 per cent pure, while some was cut with creatine powder Glynn, 63, was convicted of being concerned in the supply of heroin and cocaine by a jury in September. A judge let her walk free from court on a suspended prison sentence, telling her there was 'very little evidence of [her] having a management function in the chain or controlli He added: "You have physical ailments and your son and bereaved mother are dependent on you." Manchester Crown Court earlier heard officer swooped on Glynn's Collett Close home, in the Scholes area of the borough, in April 2021 following a tip-off that drugs were being supplied f She had lived there for 27 years. "She said she shared the property with her ex-partner... but when police entered she was there alone," prosecution barrister Craig McGregor Glynn said

Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 16:59, 10 Nov 2026 When Haider Ali started running the notorious Rochdale 'Adam' drugs line, he knew what he was in for. He'd already been jailed for dealing The £1m-a-year racket flooded the streets of the town with crack cocaine and heroin, surviving a series of police operations to bring it down In 2024, two 'untouchable' dealers were the latest to be jailed for running the line, first exposed in the BBC series The Detectives: Taking Down An OCG which shined a light on the gang, based in Newbold, Rochdale. The drugs line became active again within hours of the pair being Ali, 34, was a familiar face on the scene. He was jailed in 2015 after admitting conspiracy to supply heroin and cocaine - one of 13 dealers locked up following an undercover operation In its latest incarnation, Ali - known as 'The Ghost' - ran the 'Adam' line, until he and two others were caught. Monday (November 9), he was jailed for 10 years and six months

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport Flames shoot into sky as fire breaks out at paper recycling plant 'At one point I thought the whole thing was going to go up' Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 16:31, 10 Nov 2026 View Image The fire broke out on at Elsa Witnesses reported seeing flames shooting into the air as a fire broke out at a paper recycling plant in Stockport . Firefighters were called to Elsa Recycling on Station Road in Reddish this morning It's thought bundles of paper being stored in the yard set alight. Plumes of black smoke were pictured billowing from the blaze Station Road is also thought to have been closed while firefighters battled the flames. Witness Rob Larkin, who works nearby, said he feared the fire was going to spread He said: "The buildings are probably 20ft high and the flames were reaching that high. At one point I thought the whole thing was going to go up "You could see it was starting to spread. A second fire developed near it, but it wasn't long before the fire brigade arrived and damped it down straight away. A second appliance turned up and they took some of the bundles which had caught fire outside

candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Legal battle over GMCA skyscraper loans to be heard in Supreme Court The case is focused a decision to approve loans worth £140m in 2024 Add to preferred sources News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 15:35, 1 A legal battle over loans to a Manchester skyscraper developer will be heard in the Supreme Court The court will look at the case between Aubrey Weis and the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) over public loans to special-purpose vehicles which were part of Renaker, a Manchester property developer founded by Daren Whitaker A GMCA decision to approve the loans in 2024 unlocked £70.8m for Trinity Developments and £69.2m for New Jackson (Contour) Investments Ltd for schemes in Manchester The cash came from a scheme called the Greater Manchester Housing Investment Loans Fund (GMHILF) Previous court hearings took place in the Competition Appeal Tribunal and Court of Appeal, and questions were raised about how the loans were approved and over the interest rate

candidates.evidence_text: Courts 'Speeding' driver 'swerved and accelerated' to avoid hitting man's body in road, trial told Omar Shah denies causing Shaun Davies' death by dangerous driving Add to preferred sources News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 09:24, 10 Nov 2026 View 3 A then-20-year-old driver 'swerved and accelerated' to avoid the body of a man his cousin had just fatally struck, before driving away, a trial has heard Shaun Davies, 40, was killed in a traffic collision on Stockport Road in Ashton-under-Lyne just before midnight on April 24 2024 A trial opening at Manchester Crown Court on Monday (November 9) heard how Omar Shah's vehicle, a silver Toyota Yaris, did not make contact with Mr Davies, who was struck by a white BMW 1 series, driven by Mr Shah's cousin Bilal Shah But prosecutors have told a jury that Omar Shah 'shares the same responsibility and culpability' for Mr Davies' death as the pair were 'driving competitively' and 'racing' moments before the collision. Omar Shah, 25, of Bollington Street in Ashton-under-Lyne, denies causing death Prosecutor Colin Buckle told jurors today that the two cousins were ‘tailgating, speeding and racing’ each other on the carriageway prior to the collision, at which the speed limit is 30 miles per hour

Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

candidates.evidence_text: Russell LDP and JAG Woodford's plans for Woodford Garden Village include a grand total of 567 homes. Credit: via planning documents Councillors sided with officers on all four major applications on the planning committee’s agenda on Thursday, which was good news for Story Homes, Russell, and Bellway – and not so great for Barratt and David Wilson Homes Woodford Garden Village underwent a series of changes from its original proposals, with councillors ultimately voting in favour of the building of up to 423 homes, up to 72 fully affordable extra care apartments, and a 72-bed care home on a 75-acre site off Chester Road The plans also include 1,100 sq ft of retail space, a 6,500 sq ft health centre, and a 6,500 sq ft day nursery with outdoor space. There would also be a mobility point with cycle parking, parcel lockers, and a bus stop Russell’s plans include a 16-acre nature park that could hold nature trails, allotments, an orchard, and children’s play area. This, combined with open space allocated around the site, leads to ta total open space provision of 24.7 acres Looking at the housing plans, up to 248 homes would be affordable. This includes the 72 extra care apartments. Of those 248 homes, 22% are envisioned as social rent, 13% for affordable rent, and 65% for affordable ownership

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Two men who raped a seventeen year old have been jailed for fifteen years today after being found guilty by a unanimous jury on 30 September at Manchester Crown Court Armin Takhfifi aged 26 of Wellington Road North, Stockport and Hadi Khangheshlaghi aged 25 of Alvanley Crescent, Stockport were nineteen and eighteen respectively when the attack took place The court heard that in November 2019, the survivor, just 17 at the time, and a friend travelled to Manchester to attend a party at an Airbnb hosted by men known to one of them through university Before attending, the friend received persistent messages from one of the hosts urging her to come and bring friends After arriving at around 11pm, the girls were given drinks and a small amount of a spliff Both later described feeling overwhelmingly drowsy, weak and unable to move, a reaction they believed was far beyond what would be expected from the small amount they had consumed

candidates.evidence_text: The decision was made by just seven votes to six at a fractious planning committee meeting last night Share on WhatsApp Share via Email A visual showing the proposed Carrington Relief Road Trafford councillors have narrowly approved plans for the controversial Carrington Relief Road, despite hundreds of objections and warnings about the impact on Green Belt land and wildlife The decision was made by just seven votes to six at a fractious planning committee meeting last night, with members of the public gallery reportedly shouting "it's a disgrace" as the result was announced The road is considered essential to unlocking New Carrington, Trafford's largest housing and employment allocation, which could eventually deliver around 5,000 homes and 350,000 square metres of employment space Although the route lies around three miles north of Altrincham, the development could have wider implications for traffic, housing demand and public services across the borough The approximately 4km road would link the A6144 Manchester Road near Carrington and Partington with the Carrington Spur towards Sale

The brewery is specifically looking for a couple to take on the pub, offering a salary of £28,725 per person, a large manager's flat above the premises with all utilities paid, and free training

candidates.evidence_text: New plans to boost air quality across Manchester between now and 2040 are being brought forward by the Council Manchester’s air quality has improved significantly in recent years due to investment in public transport and cycling and walking routes, cleaner vehicle technology including electric vehicles and stricter national emissions standards. The investment-led Greater Manchester Clean But while good progress has been made, the Council wants to go further because environmental air pollution remains a real health risk, especially for people in more disadvantaged communities or with existing health conditions who can be more vulnerable to its effects The Vision is simple: “Manchester will be a city where everyone can breathe cleaner air and live healthier lives.” Alongside it sits a headline action plan which will guide further measures to improve air quality across the city, based around four priorities Reduce people’s exposure to air pollution, prioritising the most vulnerable such as children and people with existing health conditions and communities where the potential health benefits are the greatest

Nominations close at 4pm this Friday (6 November 2026) The by-election has been called following a vacancy in the ward. If there is only one candidate nominated, then that candidate would be elected without contest. If more than one valid nomination is received, residents will go to the polls on Thursday 3 December 2026 to elect thei This is an opportunity for local people from all backgrounds to represent the interests of their community, raise issues that matter to residents and play a direct role in shaping the future of Royton North and the wider borough. Councillors represent the Council to the community Anyone wishing to stand for election can obtain a nomination pack from the Elections Office at the J.R.Clynes Building, Cultural Quarter, Greaves Street, Oldham, OL1 1AL, between 9am and 5pm, or they can be emailed on request by emailing election@oldham.gov.uk Completed nomination papers must be submitted in person and cannot be accepted by email, post, fax or any other electronic method. Papers can be delivered to the J.R.Clynes Building between 10am and 4pm and no later than 4pm on Friday 6 November

candidates.lead: Primary schools have been recognised for outstanding performance in the 2026 Summer Reading Challenge Read to the Beat
candidates.evidence_text: Primary schools have been recognised for outstanding performance in the 2026 Summer Reading Challenge Read to the Beat The challenge, delivered by The Reading Agency in partnership with public libraries, encouraged children to discover the joy of reading through the theme Read to the Beat, celebrating music, rhythm and the power of stories Royton Hall Primary School, St Martin’s Primary School and Greenfield Primary School were recognised as the schools with the highest participation out of 92 schools taking part across Oldham Representatives from Oldham Libraries and partner Kajima, which supports opportunities to encourage children to read and celebrate their success, visited each school to award book tokens in recognition of pupils’ commitment to reading Kajima have sponsored the Summer Reading Challenge for the sixth year running, encouraging Oldham children towards a lifelong love of books The challenge highlights the importance of partnerships between schools, libraries and local organisations in supporting children’s literacy, building reading confidence and making reading an exciting and rewarding experience

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Primary schools have been recognised for outstanding performance in the 2026 Summer Reading Challenge Read to the Beat The challenge, delivered by The Reading Agency in partnership with public libraries, encouraged children to discover the joy of reading through the theme Read to the Beat, celebrating music, rhythm and the power of stories Royton Hall Primary School, St Martin’s Primary School and Greenfield Primary School were recognised as the schools with the highest participation out of 92 schools taking part across Oldham Representatives from Oldham Libraries and partner Kajima, which supports opportunities to encourage children to read and celebrate their success, visited each school to award book tokens in recognition of pupils’ commitment to reading Kajima have sponsored the Summer Reading Challenge for the sixth year running, encouraging Oldham children towards a lifelong love of books The challenge highlights the importance of partnerships between schools, libraries and local organisations in supporting children’s literacy, building reading confidence and making reading an exciting and rewarding experience

Rochdale firm, Winterburns, is set to take over security immediately, with a beefed up, 24-hour presence on site. The firm will also start clearing the mountain of debris which has built up over years of neglect, includin Teams will soon start the delicate internal strip out of Warwick Mill and London House. The demolition of London House, a brutalist structure with little architectural merit, is set to get under way early in the New Year

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Residents are invited to come together this November to remember and pay tribute to those who have served and sacrificed in conflicts past and present through a programme of Remembrance events The commemorations begin with the annual Concert of Remembrance at the Albert Halls on Thursday 5 November The evening will feature performances from the Shree Mukta Jeevan Swamibapa Pipe Band, Theatre Dance Studios, Phoenix Knights of Harmony, the Lancashire Artillery Military Band, and the Pipes and Drums of the 103rd Regiment The concert will also include a poignant Act of Remembrance led by the Vicar of Bolton, the Reverend Hannah Lane Tickets for the Concert of Remembrance cost £10 and are available through the Albert Halls website or by calling the box office on 0161 876 1715. All proceeds will go to Bolton’s Cadet Forces Remembrance Sunday will be marked with a civic service in Victoria Square on Sunday 8 November

A chart-topping 90s band will launch Christmas in Wigan town centre this year at a free, family-friendly Christmas lights switch-on event The event, on Sunday 22nd November, will welcome 90s pop and dance music stars D:Ream. The band, who had two top five albums in the UK charts in the mid-90s and are most known for their iconic anthems ‘Things Can Only Get Better’ and ‘U R The Best Thing’, will headline the stage The event will also feature a packed schedule of free music and entertainment, and everyone will be able to enjoy Wigan’s Christmas lights switch-on Sunday 22nd November is also the last chance to visit Light Night Wigan, a fabulous trail of beautiful light installations across Mesnes Park and town centre venues. Tickets are needed to access the Mesnes Park part of Light Night Wigan

Honouring Our Communities reflects this belief by shining a light on the people and places that have shaped our lives, identities and creative journeys. Through a collection of artworks by Black artists At HOME Arches the three artists on show are C.Talah with 'It was never just me' (2026), Damaris Edey with 'Rooted in the hands of many' (2026) and Mux Imagery with 'AYOBAMI' (2025) C. Talah (Courtney Hammond) is a Manchester-based artist whose work is inspired by identity, heritage and the people around her. Her Jamaican and British background often comes through in her work, alongside themes of family, memory and community. 'It was never just me' (2026) lo Damaris Edey is a self-taught visual artist born in Manchester, with Caribbean heritage. Her emotional portraits celebrate the divine, authentic beauty and vibrancy of Black women, while exploring the chaotic nature of life through expressive mixed media. Layers of texture create Mux Imagery is the visual practice of photographer Abiola Badmus, focusing on identity, culture, and storytelling. Through a process of reflection and catharsis the sculptures were created in carefully devised, movement informed workshops with individuals who have experience of grief. Made using tr The central space is immersed in sanguine red. Suspended moulded set plaster works produced with membrane-like hessian, appear as husks, shells, figures metamorphosed into an upturned archaeological dig; an enigmatic psychological landscape that defies the laws of physics; or cyc The duality between absence and upsurge is continued in Peake’s chalk works on paper. They are composed as double acts - still life studies of immaterial spaces between held hands, paired with drawings demonstrating gravitational or erupted motions; the dialogue between absence a Covering the central floating wall is a monumental work made from vigorous markings, engraved into thick black paper. Produced and performed in private, the enigmatic forms are instinctual. Appearing as remnants of ancient ritual or mark-making used to inscribe territory, scent o In this work notions of rotation and renewal are threaded into queered perspectives on grief, temporality and natural processes. Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

Мы решили, что новогодний корпоратив должен быть для всех! 2, 9 и 16 декабря собираемся в Mari Vanna на праздник по-домашнему, как раньше. Ёлка, огоньки, хрусталь, любимый оливье и душевное застолье. Будем петь, танцевать, получать подарки и встречать приближение Нового года! В стоимость входят праздничное застолье и развлекательная программа Выбирать и заказывать отдельные блюда не нужно. Всё меню сервируется на общий стол для вашей компании, чтобы можно было пробовать, угощаться и общаться Starters: Selection of Pickles, Russian “Olivier” salad with Veal, Meat and Fish Platters, Kholodetz with Chicken and Pork, Herring in a Shuba Coat, Selection of Russian Pirozhki (potato /cabbage/meat/mushrooms/egg and onion)

candidates.lead: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867.
candidates.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

candidates.evidence_text: Counter Manchester , the much-anticipated new restaurant from Open Restaurant Group , opens its doors today at 12pm. It is the group’s first opening in Manchester city centre and brings a theatrical approach to dining to the heart of the city Led by acclaimed chef Andrew Sheridan, Counter is located in Manchester’s Island Building on John Dalton Street and has 60 covers. It is Open Restaurant Group’s ninth restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Didsbury in Sep At the focus of the restaurant is a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, which places guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors feature four-metre elm trees, curved booth seating and a brass wine display, so the atmosphere and experienc Award-winning Andrew Sheridan brings his internationally inspired approach to Counter, building on a career that has seen multiple restaurants under his direction feature in the prestigious Michelin Guide. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander

Loungers to open Fosforo Lounge in Stretford on Saturday 28th November. By. About Manchester - . . November 9, 2026 0 . . . . . . Facebook. . Twitter. . Google+. . Pinterest. . WhatsApp. . . . . . Cadno Lounge, Neath . Loungers, the West Country‑based café‑bar group, will open Fosforo Lounge, King Street in Stretford on Saturday 28th November 2026, creating around 30 new jobs for local people.. . Fosforo Lounge will be open all day, every day, serving breakfast, brunch, lunch, dinner and drinks, with dedicated kids’, gluten‑free and vegan menus. . The site on King Street has been transformed by the Loungers design team into a warm, eclectic ‘home from home’ – their signature style. Fosforo translates to matchstick and is a nod to Manchester-based painter LS Lowry’s ‘matchstick men’ style.. . Fosforo Lounge’s all‑day menu will cater for every taste, from hearty comfort food to healthier choices and indulgent treats. Families are a major focus, with games, books, colouring materials, high chairs and baby‑changing facilities available for Little Loungers.. . With community at its heart, Fosforo Lounge will offer a welcoming space for regular meet‑ups, business catch‑ups, book clubs, knitting groups, parent‑and‑baby sessions, creative workshops and more. Local groups looking for a friendly, flexible venue will be encouraged to get in touch.. . Vix Connolly, General Manager, Fosforo Lounge said: “We’re so looking forward to welcoming everyone to Fosforo Lounge on the 28th November. Becoming a genuine part of the community is incredibly important to us, and we can’t wait to meet our neighbours and get involved locally.. . “If you’re looking for a friendly, flexible space for events or group meet‑ups, pop in once we’re open – we’d love to chat and see how we can help.”. . . . . . . New cheese festival to launch in Manchester, raising funds for The Christie Charity. By. About Manchester - . . November 11, 2026 0 . . . . . . Facebook. . Twitter. . Google+. . Pinterest. . WhatsApp. . . . . . . A new annual cheese festival will take place in Manchester this month, founded by Jonathan Pearcey AKA The Crafty Cheese Man and Track Brewing Co.. . Bringing together many of Britian and Ireland’s top artisan cheesemakers in a celebration of all things cheese , Cheese Fest will also raise funds for The Christie Charity, following Jonathan’s own experience of treatment and care through the Trust after being diagnosed with a rare form of cancer.. . Cheese Fest is free to enter and will be held at the brewery taproom from midday until 5pm. Visitors can expect stalls from award-winning cheesemakers, alongside cheese -centric food vendors and plenty of craft beer to wash it all down with, with plans already underway to make next year’s event even bigger.. . Cheesemakers in attendance will include Primrose Creamery, Wakebridge Manor Creamery, Blue Sky Halloumi, Burt’s Cheese , Larkton Hall Cheese , Mike’s Fancy Cheese , Bourne’s Cheshire Cheese and Applebys Dairy, with pizza coming in from Slice Culture, toasties from Fred’s and fermented pairings from Holly Pickles.. . While creating something special for cheese in the city of Manchester, Cheese Fest is the latest in a series of fundraising activities set up by Jonathan Pearcey for The Christie Charity, following his first hand experience of the organisation’s enhanced support for cancer patients and their families.. . Having been diagnosed with Pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP) in February 2024, an extremely rare form of cancer that can only be treated at two hospitals in the UK, Jonathan underwent a 12.5-hour operation at The Christie before having his diagnosis changed to incurable in June 2025.. . Spending 15 days in recovery at the hospital during this time, Jonathan has regularly paid tribute to the outstanding levels of care that he has received through The Christie NHS Foundation Trust, and will once again be raising funds to support services that go above and beyond what standard NHS funding can offer.. . evidence_packet.evidence_text: Hilton House keeps proving itself as one of the borough's best creative hubs and this August it's hosting a community music night. PINK's Summer Open Mic is being put on by local guitar shop Rigby Music, with covers and originals welcome from anyone who wants to give it a go Alongside the music, fellow Hilton House residents Spearpoint Vintage are setting up a pop-up of pieces from their collection, available to buy on the night, with the chance to book in for a future appointment at their showroom too It's a relaxed one — no pressure, just a room of people who like music and a rail of good vintage to pick through between sets Where: PINK, Hilton House, Lord Street, Stockport SK1 3NA When: Wednesday 5 August 2026, 6:45pm–10pm Want to perform? Email admin@rigbymusic.co.uk Know of an open mic or pop-up we should be covering? Let us know — we're always up for a Wednesday night out in the borough

candidates.lead: Posted by Manchester Digital Introducing The Inside Track: A new way to get more from your Manchester Digital membership
candidates.evidence_text: Stay connected. Know what's next. We're launching The Inside Track , a new monthly online session designed to help Manchester Digital members stay informed, discover new opportunities and make the most of their membership Whether you've recently joined Manchester Digital or have been part of our community for years, The Inside Track is your chance to catch up with our team, find out what's happening across the network and explore ways to get more involved Taking place on the last Wednesday of each month, these free, members-only sessions will bring you up to speed on the latest developments, events and opportunities across Manchester Digital, all in just 30 minutes Each session will feature a topical focus, alongside practical updates on upcoming events, programmes, speaking opportunities and ways to raise your business's profile There'll also be time to ask questions, share your priorities and find out how we can help you get more value from your membership Our first edition at midday on 25th November will focus on some of the biggest opportunities coming up across the Manchester Digital community

candidates.lead: Posted by Manchester Digital Manchester Digital Festival 2027: Programme revealed as tickets go on sale
candidates.evidence_text: Five days. Five themes. One city shaping its digital future. The first Manchester Digital Festival takes place from 8–12 February 2027 with its biggest and boldest programme yet. Manchester Digital has unveiled the programme for Manchester Digital Festival 2027 (MDF27 ) , bringin Taking place from Monday 8 to Friday 12 February 2027 , the festival marks an exciting new chapter for Manchester Digital, building on the success of Digital Skills Festival and expanding its scope to celebrate the full breadth of Greater Manchester's digital and technology secto The launch also comes as Manchester Digital celebrates its 25th anniversary , providing an opportunity to reflect on the people, businesses and innovations that have shaped the region's tech ecosystem, while looking ahead to what comes next With 15 events already announced and more to come, the first wave of the MDF27 programme offers everything from industry conferences and leadership discussions to careers events, founder stories and opportunities to explore emerging technologies Tickets for most events are now available , with further announcements expected in the coming months Under the banner Building our digital tomorrow , MDF27 introduces a new five-day format, with each day dedicated to a different theme reflecting the opportunities and challenges facing Greater Manchester's digital and technology sector

candidates.evidence_text: A special evening celebrating one of Manchester’s most influential musicians, Vini Reilly and his post-punk project The Durutti Column, comes to Albert Hall this month Fresh from sold-out Southbank Centre performances, a unique ensemble will reinterpret key works from The Durutti Column’s remarkable six-decade career in Reilly’s home city on Thu 19 Nov Presenting the one-night-only For Vini show is producer Keir Stewart, who has worked with Reilly and drummer Bruce Mitchell since 1998’s Time Was Gigantic… When We Were Kids album For the performance, Stewart (guitar, bass, samples, keys) is joined by The Durutti Column collaborators Sam Morris (French horn), Caoilfhionn Rose (vocals and piano) and Liz Rossi (violin and piano) Audiences can expect to hear material that spans releases on Factory Records through to tracks from Renascent , creating a rare and immersive live experience that honours one of Manchester’s most singular musical voices, one recently cited as a key influence on Harry Styles’ late Coinciding with the homecoming show at Albert Hall, The Durutti Column have joined with Four Tet for an official remix of Your Shadow at Morning. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A special evening celebrating one of Manchester’s most influential musicians, Vini Reilly and his post-punk project The Durutti Column, comes to Albert Hall this month Fresh from sold-out Southbank Centre performances, a unique ensemble will reinterpret key works from The Durutti Column’s remarkable six-decade career in Reilly’s home city on Thu 19 Nov Presenting the one-night-only For Vini show is producer Keir Stewart, who has worked with Reilly and drummer Bruce Mitchell since 1998’s Time Was Gigantic… When We Were Kids album For the performance, Stewart (guitar, bass, samples, keys) is joined by The Durutti Column collaborators Sam Morris (French horn), Caoilfhionn Rose (vocals and piano) and Liz Rossi (violin and piano) Audiences can expect to hear material that spans releases on Factory Records through to tracks from Renascent , creating a rare and immersive live experience that honours one of Manchester’s most singular musical voices, one recently cited as a key influence on Harry Styles’ late Coinciding with the homecoming show at Albert Hall, The Durutti Column have joined with Four Tet for an official remix of Your Shadow at Morning. candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Folk Festival is gearing up for a landmark tenth edition in March 2027, with an eclectic line-up ranging from intimate gigs by acclaimed artists to spoon-carving workshops to a Friday night ceilidh at Hallé St Peter’s Taking place over four days, from 10 – 13 March 2027, the festival will spread across six venues and outdoor spaces. Events will take place at Band on the Wall, Hallé St Peter’s, Hallé at St Michael’s, The Smithfield Market Tavern, Cutting Room Square and Stoller Hall Artists announced so far include Spiers & Boden, Eliza Carthy & The Restitution, Leveret, Catrin Finch & Aoife Ní Bhriain (pictured below), Fionn Regan (pictured above), Pokey LaFarge, Olivia Chaney, Steve Knightley, Rewild: Kantos Chamber Choir x Stevens & Pound, Spencer Cullum, And it’s not just about live music. There’ll be an intriguing programme of hands-on workshops, including spoon carving, Sacred Harp singing, corn dolly making, a sound bath and drop-in sketch sessions A festival wristband will give you access to all the shows, as well as to an exclusive Jim Moray concert just for wristband holders. You’ll also be invited to the opening day celebrations with music across three stages at Stoller Hall Earlybird wristbands sold out in record time. Second-release wristbands are now on sale, with the next price increase due in late November, so secure yours now to get the best value. You can also buy individual concert tickets for headline shows

Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC JJ Gabriel comment ‘shocks Real Madrid’ as concern raised about Man United star’s dad JJ Gabriel looks set to complete a move from Manchester United to Real Madrid in a blow to the club Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Amie Wilson Sports Real Madrid are reportedly surprised by comments from JJ Gabriel ahead of his move to the club. There are also said to be concerns about his father's demanding reputation in the Spanish capital The 16-year-old was highly rated at Manchester United , having impressed throughout his progress in the academy. He was seen as the next player ready to make the step up to first-team action So the youngster left the Reds stunned back in September when he asked to be deregistered from the club . He has since held talks with both Barcelona and Real Madrid In comments to Spanish outlet Marca, Gabriel, and his dad, former professional Joe O’Cearuill, pretty much confirmed the move to the Bernabéu . United sources say that they are yet to recieve any contact from the Spanish giants Get the best United news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the Manchester Evening News!

Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. Скільки концертів зіграли, скільки грошей зібрали, які пісні видали. Це база. Непогано ще пам’ятати, чи був гурт у країні, до якої ми збираємося, чи це пер О, як би хотілося написати: "Концерт гурту Бумбокс" — і як у Львові за добу продано 8000 квитків. Так-так, ми не про Львів розповідаємо, хоча теж про Європу Наші віддані слухачі, якщо ви перебуваєте за кордоном, сподіваємось, вам буде цікаво дізнатися, що після традиційної перерви на декілька місяців, Бумбокс поїде в турне від Ізраїлю до Німеччини, від Англії до Польщі, від Ірландії до Словаччини та Чехії І повеземо ми в це турне свіженький, як херсонський кавун, максі-сингл “Живий”, підсилений піснями з різних альбомів, під частину яких виросли ви, а під частину зростають ваші діти Тож ознайомтеся, будь ласка, уважно з розкладом туру, купуйте квитки заздалегідь, готуйте гроші на донати та мерч — зустрінемося в листопаді

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Приготовьтесь к незабываемому вечеру с одной из самых любимых звезд турецкой поп-сцены — Муратом Далкылычем, в Лондоне! Он известен своим узнаваемым голосом, энергичными выступлениями и популярными песнями, среди которых «Bir Güzellik Yap». За годы карьеры в музыке, написании песен и кино он прио 29 января 2027 года Мурат Далкылыч выступит в indigo at The O2 в Лондоне. Вас ждет яркий вечер турецкой поп-музыки, живого исполнения и любимых хитов Не упустите возможность увидеть Мурата Далкылыча вживую в Лондоне!
